title: Garbage
creator: rblevin
content:
I have used and use Thunderbird on the desktop for decades. It's my primary email application. I've donated to support Module.

I installed the mobile app on my Galaxy Z Fold 7 and connected it to two email accounts: Gmail and my own domain.

My experience has been terrible.

Connecting to Outlook specifically was impossible. The app and Outlook were utterly confused and couldn't authenticate.

Conversation view doesn't work.

Notifications don't work.

Email shows up in the Gmail but not Thunderbird.

With conversation enabled, not only can't you read email as conversations, but basic email history/threads don't appear in messages. If you disable conversation view, then they appear. (That was the biggest warning sign that this app is in trouble.)

I could go on. Using Thunderbird Mobile is like living in the Bizarro universe. IIt pains me to say it, but that's been my experience.

I'm a highly experienced user and developer. I've checked all the settings and rechecked. It ain't me. It's the app.

Uninstalling.

title: after IMAP server content edit, have to clear local messages, and there's a bug.
creator: john1260
content:
to recreate the issue.. edit IMAP server content, go to existing account on phone and see that latest messages are not in inbox (they are where expected on webmail and TB[win] desktop).

no manner of refresh, load more, clearing app cache & data, uninstalling and rebooting, reinstalling, import settings, or manual settings will restore the correct inbox list. Only the below, and only with the step of local folder size: all, and the following bug of things not changing back to 100 with that further step. Other android mail apps do not have the issue on the same email account.

left hamburger > select account > settings > account settings > fetching mail > local folder size > change to all > accept. back > back > back > manage folders > inbox > triple dot > clear local messages > clear messages. back > back > settings > account settings > fetching mail > local folder size > change to 100 > accept. back > back > back > dismiss side panel menu > load up to 100 more. That loads in the ENTIRE inbox, not just the recent 100, but the list of messages is at least correct.

I resorted to offline archiving older messages with TB[win] desktop to shrink the server inbox sizes, and thankfully I do have plenty of room at the moment on my phone.

it seems that the android app has some cache or local database that does not clear except with the "clear local messages" - and it does so with a setting bug. Android security doesnt allow me to access the root folders of thunderbird on the device, and connecting the phone to pc with usb doesnt give access to that directory either.

android v15. A dovecot index rebuild is not a good answer - as ONLY TB Android is affected.
